DATA DISCREPANCY: the two intake forms disagree on the combined existing loan payoff — Holcomb form states $216k, Kingsford form states $217k; Keith confirmed $217,000 is the correct figure to use (08/24/26). Kingsford: property type/unit count still not specified (units defaulted to 1 for quoting), 3/2 bed-bath, tenant-occupied, market rent $1,500 (current contract rent $990/mo through 7/31/27), annual taxes $3,000, annual insurance $2,000, HOA $0. Per Keith's direction, quoted as BOTH individual (single-asset) loans AND an indicative portfolio/blanket structure — 6 quotes total, 2 lenders x 3 structures. CRITICAL FINDING (contract rent, $990/mo/property): this deal is severely DSCR-constrained on both properties — sizing at the standard 75% LTV comparison headline FAILS DSCR eligibility on every single structure (both lenders, both individual and portfolio). Loan amounts in the quotes below are each sized to the maximum that clears a 1.00 DSCR (the realistic ceiling) at CONTRACT rent, not 75% LTV. Even the best-case structure (indicative portfolio, Option A/6.375%) tops out at $183,150 — $33,850 SHORT of the $217,000 payoff Travis needs, with no cash-out possible. Splitting into two individual Option A loans is worse ($91,900 + $86,450 = $178,350 combined, $38,650 short). SECOND FINDING (08/24/26, market rent $1,500/property): re-run at Travis's own stated market rent figures ($1,500/property, $3,000/mo combined) instead of contract rent — this clears DSCR comfortably on every structure at 75% LTV: Kingsford $150,000 (Option A 7.000%/DSCR 1.06 PASS, Option B 7.500%/DSCR 1.02 PASS); Holcomb $99,750 (Option A 7.125%/DSCR 1.38 PASS, Option B 8.125%/DSCR 1.30 PASS); portfolio (indicative) $249,750 (Option A 6.875%/DSCR 1.21 PASS, Option B 7.625%/DSCR 1.15 PASS). Combined at 75% LTV = $249,750 either way (individual sum or portfolio) — $32,750 MORE than the $217,000 payoff, enough to cover payoff plus most rolled-in closing costs. Option A can stretch to 80% LTV on Holcomb/portfolio (Kingsford alone fails DSCR at 80%, 0.99); Option B tops out at 75% regardless — its rate grid doesn't offer a 75-80% band at a 680 FICO. CAVEAT — NOT CURRENTLY QUALIFIABLE: both units are under signed 12-month leases at $990/mo through 7/31/27, and DSCR programs standardly qualify off the LOWER of contract or market rent, not market rent outright, absent an expiring lease or vacancy. So the market-rent scenario is what this deal could support once the leases turn over and re-lease at market — not something to quote to Travis as available today. THIRD FINDING (08/24/26, CONTRACT rent $990/mo/property, 5-YEAR INTEREST-ONLY): re-run at contract rent using a 5yr IO structure (interest-only payment, no principal, on both engines) instead of 30-year amortizing — IO lowers the qualifying payment and meaningfully raises the DSCR-capped max loan, though it still doesn't fully close the gap. At 75% LTV IO still FAILS DSCR on every structure (Kingsford CV3 0.77/BPL 0.72, Holcomb CV3 0.94/BPL errors at the 65% band cap, portfolio CV3 0.84/BPL errors). DSCR-capped max with IO: Kingsford $107,500 (Option A, 6.375%, DSCR 1.00) / $91,733 (Option B, 7.500%, DSCR 1.00); Holcomb $94,897 (Option A, 7.250%, DSCR 1.00) / $86,450 (Option B, 7.875%, DSCR 1.01); portfolio (indicative) $211,692 (Option A, 6.500%, DSCR 1.00) / $193,123 (Option B, 7.125%, DSCR 1.00) — vs. $183,150/$174,550 on the 30yr amortizing structure, so IO adds roughly $28,542 (portfolio, Option A) over amortizing. BEST CASE OVERALL: portfolio, Option A, 5yr IO, $211,692 — only $5,308 SHORT of the $217,000 payoff, close enough that a modest cash contribution from Travis, a slightly lower final payoff, or reduced rolled-in closing costs could realistically bridge it. Combined individual IO loans (best lender each, both Option A): $107,500 + $94,897 = $202,397 — $14,603 short, worse than the portfolio route. Flagged to Keith before any term sheet goes to Travis — nothing sent to the borrower yet pending his direction (wait for lease turnover vs. bring cash to cover the contract-rent shortfall vs. 5yr IO portfolio structure plus a modest cash contribution vs. explore whether a lender will accept a documented rent survey sooner). FOURTH FINDING (08/25/26, OFFICIAL CV3 SIZER — SUPERSEDES the CV3 5yr-IO figures in the THIRD FINDING above, individual/single-asset only): re-ran both properties as two separate single-asset CV3 loans, 5/6 (5yr IO) term, using Keith's uploaded official CV3 'Pricing Tool v3.04.2' Rental Loan Sizer rather than the standalone engine. Two critical mechanics discovered in the official sizer (now logged in house-rules.md under 'Confirmed pricing mechanics'): (1) a 5/6 IO loan is qualified off the FULLY AMORTIZING payment, not the IO payment — choosing IO lowers the borrower's actual payment but does NOT raise the DSCR-qualifying loan size, contrary to the standalone engine's IO=True assumption; (2) CV3 hard-gates any DSCR<1.00 loan at a 700 FICO minimum, at any LTV/amount — Travis's 680 FICO means both properties are hard-capped at whatever loan size clears DSCR ≥ 1.00 on the amortizing payment, full stop. Official-sizer results: Kingsford Ave capped at $88,600 (44.3% LTV) at 6.625%, DSCR 1.0061; Holcomb Rd capped at $84,455 (63.5% LTV) at 7.125%, DSCR 1.0044 — both driven by the 680 FICO/DSCR-1.00 floor, not LTV headroom. COMBINED (2 individual CV3 loans): $173,055 — $43,945 SHORT of the $217,000 payoff, meaningfully worse than the THIRD FINDING's standalone-engine individual-IO estimate ($202,397 combined) because that estimate incorrectly assumed IO relaxes DSCR sizing. The official sizer is the authoritative source per house rules (trumps the standalone engine whenever both are available) — treat $173,055 (individual) as the real ceiling for this structure, not the $202,397 figure quoted earlier. Two completed sizer files (FINAL_Kingsford_CV3_5-6IO.xlsx, FINAL_Holcomb_CV3_5-6IO.xlsx) delivered to Keith 08/25/26. Portfolio/blanket structure not re-verified against an official sizer (CV3's engines and sizer are single-asset only) — the THIRD FINDING's $211,692 indicative portfolio figure is unverified against official tooling and should be treated with added caution given how far off individual-IO sizing was. Reason logged as 'Other' since the standard loss-reason list (beaten on rate/terms, declined our terms, paid cash, wanted higher LTC) doesn't have a dedicated 'lost on timing' option. FLAG — corrected a borrower claim that did NOT hold up against the source documents: the borrower's email said 144/146 S Bryant 'broadly do not have fully updated mechanical, new roofs, or all new flooring' like the subject — but both MLS listings' own remarks describe extensive renovations including updated kitchens, baths, mechanical systems, and flooring, closely comparable to the subject's 2023 renovation. Keith does not want the reconsideration/any follow-up appraisal handled by the same appraiser (Northtowne Appraisal Services, Ltd.) — flagged as overly conservative.
